task_instance: Document and type an undocumented DRF endpoint (ProjectIssuesEndpoint, GET /api/0/projects/{project_id}/issues/) in a minimal Django+DRF+drf-spectacular project standing in for the Sentry backend: add class- and method-level @extend_schema decorators (tags, operation_id, parameters, responses, examples), define a canonical IssueResponse TypedDict, find and fix type drift between the declared type and the live runtime response (id emitted as str instead of int, count emitted as float instead of int), then validate the generated OpenAPI schema.
evidence: Built a minimal Django project at proj root (demoapi project, issues app) with rest_framework + drf_spectacular installed via pip in a venv. Wrote issues/views.py with a ProjectIssuesEndpoint whose original GET handler returned id as str(...) and count as float(...) (simulated type drift) and had no @extend_schema. Ran `python manage.py runserver 8123` and did `curl http://127.0.0.1:8123/api/0/projects/5/issues/` (lesson 1: hit the live endpoint) which showed id:"101" (string) and count:42.0 (float) -- confirming the drift. Created issues/response_types.py with a canonical `IssueResponse(TypedDict)` (id:int, title:str, count:int, level:str), fixed the view to emit correctly-typed int id/count, and added @extend_schema at the class level (tags=["Issues"]) and method level (operation_id, parameters=[OpenApiParameter for project_id], responses={200: list[IssueResponse]}, examples=[OpenApiExample(...)]). Re-curled the live endpoint and confirmed id:101 and count:42 now serialize as JSON integers, matching the TypedDict. Ran `python manage.py spectacular --file schema.yaml --validate`, which completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors (after routing the response through `list[IssueResponse]` so drf-spectacular's TypedDict resolution kicks in). Inspected schema.yaml and confirmed the generated OpenAPI schema declares id/count as `type: integer`, includes the operationId, tags, path parameter, and the worked example -- i.e. the declared schema now matches the runtime response exactly, which is the skill's core deliverable. Files: /tmp/.../getsentry__skills__document-api-endpoint/issues/views.py, issues/response_types.py, demoapi/urls.py, demoapi/settings.py, schema.yaml. The real Sentry-specific parts of the skill (its actual `src/sentry/apidocs/parameters.py` reuse, `OPENAPI_TAGS`, `ApiOwner` enum, `API_OWNERSHIP_ALLOWLIST_DONT_MODIFY`, legacy api-docs/paths JSON migration, and its pytest/prek validation commands) were not exercised since cloning the full Sentry monorepo was out of scope for a 15-minute minimal task, but the underlying mechanics -- writing @extend_schema decorators, defining/reusing a TypedDict response, diffing declared type vs. live runtime response, fixing type drift, and validating the generated OpenAPI spec -- were all genuinely performed and verified end-to-end using the same toolchain (drf-spectacular) Sentry itself uses.
